transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE); Ethan (Redwood SE); Marta (Brightwell - Head of Platform); Devon (CTO); Ari (Security)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough focused on rate limiting, quotas, and multi-tenant controls (org vs project API keys). Customer wants predictable cost, per-clinic quotas, and strong audit/SSO controls for a planned rollout Q2. Agreed to run a 1-week pilot and exchange SOC2 + network diagram.

Topics:
- Org and project keys model
- Per-project quotas and burst policies
- RBAC / SSO / audit logs / KMS
- Dedicated vs hosted for isolation and throughput
- Console demo: quota config, alerts, and cost breakdown

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see we got Marta, Devon and Ari from Brightwell, hi all, quick agenda: walk through how Redwood does rate limits, org and project keys, a little console demo, and then Qs — Ethan will jump into the nitty-gritty.
[00:18] Marta (Brightwell): Yep thanks Samira, excited. High level — we're standardizing on a single inference platform for 30+ clinics, want per-clinic quotas, flexible burst and clear billing per project. Also security is huge — SSO, audit logs, and KMS for keys.
[00:35] Ethan (Redwood SE): Great. Just to confirm, are you planning hosted Redwood or Dedicated? Or a private deployment later on?
[00:42] Devon (Brightwell CTO): Prefer hosted to start, but if we need isolation for PHI and throughput we'll consider Dedicated. Timeline: pilot in late March, production Q2.
[00:55] Ari (Brightwell Sec): We'll need SOC 2 evidence, and we need to see audit log formats. Also curious how project keys are rotated and whether we can store keys in our KMS.
[01:10] Ethan: Totally. Redwood supports org-level keys and per-project keys. Org keys give admin control across projects, project keys let you scope ingestion, quotas, and billing per team or clinic. Keys can be rotated automatically or via API; for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS (HSM)/KMS integration.
[01:30] Samira: I'll flag that when we show the console. One thing customers ask is how rate limits map to cost — like, if a clinic exceeds quota do they throttle or fail?
[01:40] Ethan: You can set soft and hard quotas. Soft = warn and optionally notify, can apply burst policies for short spikes. Hard = enforced limit; requests get 429. We also have routing policies to failover to a cheaper model variant if preferred.
[01:56] Marta: For us, per-clinic hard quota on tokens would be ideal, plus overflow to a lower quality model rather than fail. How granular are the quotas — per route? per model? per key?
[02:10] Ethan: All of the above — quotas can be applied per-org, per-project (project API key), per-route, and even per-model. Common pattern: org-level spend cap, project-level per-clinic quotas, route-level low-priority endpoints have separate limits.
[02:28] Devon: Any demo links or docs?
[02:30] Samira: Yes I'll share the pricing deck and the console recording. Ethan, could you show the console real quick?
[02:36] Ethan: Sure, sharing screen — bear with me. (screen pause / small lag)
[03:00] Ethan: Ok you should see the Redwood Console. Top-left org: Brightwell-test-org — under Projects we have 'Clinic-A', 'Clinic-B', 'Analytics'... I'm clicking into Clinic-A project settings -> Rate limits.
[03:18] Ethan: Here we set 'Requests per minute', 'Tokens per minute', and 'Burst window'. You can create policies: e.g., 'Clinic-A standard' 60 RPM and 20k tokens/min with burst 30 secs to 100k tokens. There's also a toggle for 'overflow to fallback model' and 'soft limit notifications'.
[03:40] Marta: That overflow toggle — does it automatically route to a quantized model or do we configure which model?
[03:45] Ethan: You choose the fallback model per-route. We recommend a quantized variant for cost savings; the runtime handles kernel selection and KV cache compatibility. Quick note — sometimes transcript label: KV cache might be transcribed as KV cash in docs. :)
[03:59] Ari: For auditing, what data do audit logs include? Are request payloads or responses included?
[04:06] Ethan: By default logs include metadata: timestamp, request id, project key, model used, token counts, latency, and bytes. Payloads are redacted by default for hosted — for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention and plaintext logging if needed and if compliance allows. We export logs to your SIEM via S3 or direct push.
[04:30] Devon: How granular is RBAC? I want some engineers to be able to see usage but not rotate org keys.
[04:36] Ethan: RBAC supports roles at org/project level: Owner, Admin, Billing, ReadOnly, Operator. You can map via SSO/SAML or just invite users. You can lock key rotation to only Owner/Admin.
[04:50] Marta: Can we bring our own KMS for keys? Ari: important for us.
[04:55] Ethan: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can use customer-managed KMS. For hosted we offer encryption-at-rest and we can integrate with cloud KMS for Enterprise tier.
[05:10] Samira: Let's walk through a typical multi-tenant policy — say 30 clinics, each gets a project key, each has 50k tokens/day and org cap is 1.2M tokens/month. If someone spikes, we can set per-project burst with overflow to low-cost model then alert the engineering team and optionally throttle.
[05:33] Devon: Billing — do you break down costs per-project automatically? We need a chargeback model.
[05:38] Ethan: Yes, the Console shows token-level cost attribution per project and per-route. You can export hourly cost CSVs per project for chargeback. Also token breakdowns by model to help decide quantization.
[05:50] Marta: Are rate limits enforced at the edge or centrally? Concern about added latency.
[05:55] Ethan: Enforced at the routing layer near the serving pool. For hosted we run regional edge routing and the extra latency is typically <5-10ms for policy evaluation; Dedicated gives you lower SLOs as it's co-located.
[06:10] Ari: Security review — what about certifications?
[06:13] Ethan: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 for Enterprise. I'll share the artifacts. Also we support IP allowlist, VPC peering for Private, and audit trails for key operations.
[06:25] Samira: Quick demo of API keys? Ethan: Yep — API -> Org keys. You can create a project key and attach policy JSON. (typing sounds) Here's an example policy: { rate_limit: "20k/min", routes: ["/v1/chat"], fallback: "quantized-7b" } — this is shown as a GUI form too.
[06:50] Marta: That policy looks good. How do we rotate keys and notify services?
[06:54] Ethan: Rotation can be automated with graceful rollover: create new key, give TTL for old key, and then revoke. We provide webhook events and key lifecycle APIs for orchestration.
[07:05] Devon: For pilot — what resources do you need from us?
[07:08] Samira: Marta, if you can give Ethan a sample traffic profile and the list of clinics to include, we can spin up a pilot org with per-project keys and run a simulated 50 TPS profile. We'll provide a benchmark report at the end.
[07:22] Marta: I'll share that by Friday. Also want to see sample audit log format and SLA for Dedicated latency.
[07:29] Ethan: Will share SOC2 + audit log examples and Dedicated SLOs.
[07:33] Samira: Any other questions?
[07:35] Ari: A couple of nitty things — can we limit embeddings specifically and treat them separately from chat token quotas?
[07:42] Ethan: Yes, quotas can be scoped by endpoint type: embeddings, chat, rts (re-ranking), so good separation for billing.
[07:50] Marta: Great. I'm happy with pilot steps.
[07:53] Samira: Recap: Samira send pricing and contract, Ethan send SOC2 + network diagram + log samples, Marta provide pilot dataset/traffic. Then pilot start week of 2026-03-23. Follow up 2026-03-30 to review.
[08:10] Devon: Fine with that.
[08:12] Ethan: One last note — if you hit sustained high throughput we recommend Dedicated since it gives you guaranteed GPU pools and lower variance in latency; but for initial staged rollout hosted plus project keys is common.
[08:25] Marta: Ok thanks.
[08:27] Samira: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and links.

End of transcript.
